STORY BRIEF
- Protagonist: A shy café owner who can hear what people's coffee orders really mean
- Goal: Save the café from closing before the cherry blossom festival
- Genre: Slice of Life
- World rule (must matter to the plot): The gift only works on strangers, never on people she loves
- Ending twist (reveal near the climax, set it up earlier): The rival café owner was her childhood pen pal all along
- Tone: light and hopeful (90/100 toward light)
- Conflict level: low (30/100)
- Romance: central (90/100)
- Action intensity: low (10/100)
- Length: 4 chapters of about 270 words each

  "title": string,
  "logline": string (2-3 sentence teaser),
  "characters": [{"name": string, "role": "protagonist"|"ally"|"rival"|"villain"|"mentor"|"other",
                  "visual_description": string (hair, eyes, outfit; reused for every image)}]  (3-5 items),
  "relationships": [{"source": name, "target": name, "label": short string like "ALLY", "CONFLICT"}],
  "beats": [{"name": one of "Inciting Incident","Call to Action","Rising Conflict","Midpoint Turn","Climax","Resolution",
             "summary": one sentence}]  (exactly 6, in that order),

}

chapters.title: Bitter Beans and Quiet Hopes
chapters.text: Hana wiped down the wooden counter of her cozy shop, The Daily Blossom, listening to the heavy silence of an empty room. Outside, spring petals drifted past the window, but inside, financial worries weighed down the air. She possessed a strange, quiet gift: whenever a stranger ordered a drink, she heard their true emotional subtext. When a tired salaryman asked for a black coffee, she heard, I just want someone to tell me I am doing a good job. Hana quietly slipped a warm, complimentary pastry into his bag with a handwritten note of encouragement. He smiled, and for a fleeting moment, the café felt alive. Yet, her ledger showed the bitter truth. If business did not pick up before the upcoming cherry blossom festival in two weeks, she would have to close her doors forever. Her loyal employee Mei squeezed her shoulder gently, offering a bright, optimistic grin. They needed a miracle, or at least a lot more customers, to keep the dream alive.

chapters.title: The Rival Across the Street
chapters.text: The miracle did not arrive; instead, a sleek new competitor named Artisan Brew opened directly across the cobblestone street. Its owner was Ren, a handsome man with sharp blue eyes and a notoriously perfectionist attitude. Ren often stood outside his shop, watching Hana with an unreadable expression that made her nervous. When Hana walked over to inspect her new neighbor, Ren ordered a simple espresso. Hana braced herself to listen for his true intentions, expecting arrogance or dismissal. But to her utter shock, nothing happened. The gift of subtext remained completely silent. She blinked in confusion, wondering if her strange magic was finally breaking down. Later, Mei teased her about how long she had stared at the rival owner. Hana blushed, insisting it was professional concern, but her heart fluttered strangely. Ren was a stranger, yet her heart stubbornly refused to classify him as one. How could her magical safety net fail precisely when she needed to read her biggest opponent the most?

chapters.title: Letters in the Attic
chapters.text: Desperate for answers, Hana spent her evening sorting through old childhood boxes in her attic. She stumbled upon a faded shoebox filled with letters from her childhood pen pal, a boy who had shared her love for cherry blossoms and specialty teas. They had lost touch years ago when he moved away. As she read through the affectionate, poetic handwriting, a sudden shiver ran down her spine. The phrasing, the wry humor, and the specific references to coffee bean roasting styles sounded remarkably familiar. She held a letter up to the moonlight, her mind racing back to the man across the street. Could it be? The next morning, Hana marched over to Artisan Brew before opening hours. Ren was sweeping his porch, looking softer in the morning light. She pulled a weathered letter from her apron pocket and held it out to him silently. Ren stopped sweeping, his breath catching in his throat as he stared at the familiar pale blue stationery.

chapters.title: Blossoms and Brews
chapters.text: Ren looked up from the letter, a genuine, unguarded smile breaking across his face—the very smile Hana remembered from childhood drawings. 'You kept them,' he whispered, tossing his broom aside. He confessed that he had opened his shop nearby specifically hoping to reconnect with her, mistaking her polite distance for lingering childhood resentment. The magical silence made complete sense now; her heart had recognized him long before her conscious mind did. With the misunderstanding cleared, they decided to merge their shops for the cherry blossom festival. On the day of the festival, the street was packed with laughing crowds sipping sakura lattes under a canopy of pink petals. Inside the newly unified café, Hana handed Ren a cup of chamomile tea. He whispered, I love you, and this time, she did not need magical subtext to know he meant every single word.
